description.value: A proposed 9-month longitudinal fMRI study examining brain activation during food-cue viewing in obese and healthy weight participants before and after a 12-week weight-loss intervention, and identifying brain activation predictors of weight loss and weight maintenance.

spans.text: This study will use neuroimaging in participants while viewing food and non-food images.

value: We hypothesize that obese, relative to healthy weight; individuals will show greater activation to food pictures in limbic and paralimbic brain regions, both before and after eating.

We hypothesize that individuals who lose more weight will show greater reductions in activation, from the baseline to follow-up sessions, in limbic and paralimbic brain regions in comparison to unsuccessful dieters and healthy weight controls.
We hypothesize that fMRI activation in limbic and paralimbic regions taken from the Baseline Session scans will be significantly correlated with subsequent weight loss in obese subjects.

We hypothesize that individuals who successfully maintain weight loss will show reduced activation in limbic and paralimbic brain regions, in comparison to the other obese groups and healthy weight controls.
We hypothesize that fMRI measures of activation in limbic and paralimbic regions taken from the follow-up scan will be correlated with weight maintenance and weight regain.
